key_insight: A label-free physics-informed neural network can estimate slope failure under spatially variable strength reduction, and a neural operator can then generalize those solutions to predict reliability at massive scale.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast probabilistic slope stability assessment without running finite-element simulations for every random field, while still matching Abaqus factor of safety and failure zones closely enough for engineering screening.
method: PINN solves non-associated Mohr-Coulomb plasticity with a virtual-work loss on the FE mesh
Incremental strength reduction is used to estimate factor of safety across many random fields on GPU
A neural operator learns from PINN outputs to predict factor of safety, displacement path, and failure mode for many fields quickly
evidence_signal: On 52 random fields, the PINN reproduced Abaqus factor of safety within about 2–3% RMS and identified the same weak-zone failure mechanisms; the operator was then trained to predict a million fields in seconds.
watch_item: The reported reliability is sensitive to small factor-of-safety errors and is tied to one mesh, so the under-resolved plastic strain band and mesh dependence should be checked before design use.
paper_title: Label-free physics-informed strength reduction and a neural operator for the reliability of spatially variable slopes
